purpose: What the filings of the corpus say about a syndicate's own run-off, year by year (the author's decision of 1 October 2026, option A; round 62, fourth cycle). One entry per syndicate-year whose filing speaks of the syndicate itself running off or ceasing to underwrite, read from the filing's own words and classified by them. The whole-year run-off rule reads the WHOLE entries; the others are kept so that every reading is on record and a reader can see what was not counted, and why. An entry is classified only as far as the filing's words go: where they do not settle it the entry is NOTCOUNT and its note says so. A legacy vehicle (a syndicate that takes on other syndicates' liabilities by reinsurance to close or loss portfolio transfer) that says it is in run-off is WHOLE like any other; whether the analysis keeps it is for the analysis's assumed-business regime, not for this register.

categories.WHOLE: the filing states that the syndicate is in run-off, or has ceased underwriting, from the start of the year or before: a run-off year
categories.PART: the run-off begins during the year (runoff_from says when): the syndicate was underwriting for part of it
categories.AFTER: the run-off begins at or after the year end: the syndicate was underwriting during the year
categories.NOTCOUNT: not counted as a run-off year: the filing's words do not settle it (the note says why), or the statement is about another entity

premium_register: pdf_extraction/audit/runoff_register.json holds the premium rule's own readings (records with a development figure and a premium at or below zero). Eight of its entries are also entries here and are copies of it; tests/test_runoff_corpus_register.py fails if the two differ. 3623/2018, the one premium-register record that is no entry here, is a live syndicate.

records.note: In run-off, on the author's reading of this filing's own account (30 September 2026). Its Future developments statement (the evidence; pdf page 10, printed 6) says the syndicate 'continues to run-off its portfolio of liabilities' and that the 2013 year of account was reinsured to close into 2015 'for administrative purposes only'. The filing names a Syndicate Run-off Manager (pdf page 6, printed 2), says no RITC contracts of Lloyd's syndicates were underwritten in 2015 (pdf page 7, printed 3) and prints a gross premium written of (362) thousand pounds, the negative premium the record adopted (pdf page 16, printed 12); all three fit that account. Four passages could be read the other way and are recorded so that a reader sees all of them. The going concern paragraph (pdf page 21, printed 17) is the standard going concern statement of the basis of preparation and is not read as saying that the syndicate underwrites new business; it reads, verbatim: 'Having taken into account the risks and uncertainties and the performance of the syndicate as disclosed in the Report of the directors and making inquiries, the managing agent has a reasonable expectation that the syndicate will continue to write business for the foreseeable future. Moreover, the managing agent expects that continued capital support will be in place in order to do so. Accordingly, the financial statements have been prepared on the going concern basis.' The Statement of Managing Agent's Responsibilities (pdf page 13, printed 9) says the accounts are prepared on the basis that the syndicate 'will continue to write future business unless it is inappropriate to presume the syndicate will do so'. The Future developments paragraph itself ends 'Syndicate 2255 will continue to search for and evaluate suitable new business propositions.' and the income statement ends 'All operations are continuing.' (pdf page 16, printed 12). The syndicate is a reinsurance-to-close vehicle: it commenced underwriting on 1 January 2011 and was set up to underwrite the RITC of Lloyd's syndicates (pdf page 7, printed 3), and in 2011 it wrote the RITC of Syndicate 1861 (2008 and prior) and of Syndicate 340 (1998 to 2001) (pdf page 8, printed 4).

reviewed_not_run_off.evidence: The principal activity of Syndicate 1110 is the transaction of reinsurance business in the United Kingdom by way of reinsurance to close (“RITC”), loss portfolio transfer (“LPT”) or adverse development cover (“ADC”).

other_statements.quote: Gross premium has reduced from £333.4m to £5.6m due to no deals occurring in the year.

The Syndicate continues to pursue reinsurance business opportunities in the United Kingdom by way of reinsurance to close (“RITC”), loss portfolio transfer (“LPT”) or adverse development cover (“ADC”).

reviewed_not_run_off.reason: The filing does not say the syndicate is in run-off. It describes a legacy consolidator whose principal activity is reinsurance to close, loss portfolio transfer and adverse development cover business, that wrote no deals in 2023 (gross premium 5.6m against 333.4m) and says it continues to pursue them. Its 2024 filing (syndicate_1110_2024, PART) puts the run-off in July 2024. On the filing's words the syndicate was not in run-off in 2023.
